The source result includes mu=L, while Appendix B Lemma 4 uses denominators L−mu without an explicit endpoint treatment in the read material. The source statement is faithfully retained; independent endpoint reproof is not claimed.

map: p.7 defines T^k=(1/n)sum_i [f_i(phi_i^k)−f_i(x*)−<grad f_i(x*),phi_i^k−x*>]+c||x^k−x*||^2, with c=1/[2 gamma (1−gamma mu)n] and kappa=1/(gamma mu).
Uniform replacement gives the two table expectation recurrences on p.7. Proximal nonexpansiveness and the optimality fixed point x*=prox_gamma^h(x*−gamma grad f(x*)) bound the iterate-distance term.

p.7 expands the square and uses the centering identity. Appendix B Lemma 7 p.11 derives the variance bound using the PLUS-centered square and variance decomposition; Lemmas 4–6 pp.10–11 supply smooth/strongly convex and stored-gradient bounds. Printed Lemma 3/7 statements display a minus sign; the adopted PLUS-centered convention is recorded separately below.

p.8 combines these estimates into Eq.(10), invoking the cited smooth strongly convex gradient inequality [13, Theorem 2.1.10]. With gamma=1/[2(mu n+L)], beta=(2mu n+L)/L, the stated c and kappa, the remaining coefficients are nonpositive. Theorem 1 states the conditional contraction E[T^(k+1)|history]≤(1−1/kappa)T^k.

p.8 Corollary 1 uses c||x^k−x*||^2≤T^k, chains expectations, substitutes the fully initialized T^0, and simplifies the initial-divergence coefficient using mu(n−0.5)≤mu n to obtain the recorded bound.

assumptions: Every f_i is differentiable, mu-strongly convex and has L-Lipschitz gradient on R^d, with the same 0<mu≤L.
h is scalar convex; the proximal minimizer used at every step is well-defined and computed exactly.
F attains its minimum at x*. x^0∈R^d is fixed and all initial component gradients are queried at x^0.
Each sampled index is uniform conditional on the past. Use gamma=1/[2(mu n+L)] and the old table mean in the correction.
statement.conclusion: E||x^k−x*||^2 ≤ (1−mu/[2(mu n+L)])^k [||x^0−x*||^2 + n D_f(x^0,x*)/(mu n+L)]. This is the displayed strongly convex bound in Section 2 p.2 and Corollary 1 p.8.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let n,d be positive integers, f_i:R^d→R, f=(1/n)sum_i f_i and F=f+h. Let x* minimize F. Let ||.|| be Euclidean. Define D_f(x^0,x*)=f(x^0)−f(x*)−<grad f(x*),x^0−x*>. Initialize a_i^0=grad f_i(x^0) for every i. At step k draw j uniformly conditional on history, set v^k=grad f_j(x^k)−a_j^k+(1/n)sum_i a_i^k, x^(k+1)=prox_gamma^h(x^k−gamma v^k), and replace only a_j by grad f_j(x^k). Here prox_gamma^h(y)=argmin_z {h(z)+||z−y||^2/(2gamma)}.
statement.parameter_domains: n,d∈positive integers; L>0; 0<mu≤L; k∈nonnegative integers; gamma=1/[2(mu n+L)].
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such fixed instance and initialization, and every integer k≥0, the conclusion holds with expectation over all sampled indices through the first k updates. x* is fixed; this is not a high-probability or pathwise assertion.
